where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (_checker_program_word, used by test_grammar_checker_agrees_with_the_allow_list); the rule is the program alternative of _CALL_TEXT_RE in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py; the grammar is in rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md
problem: The independent checker was meant to follow caller-identity.md sentence by sentence. At one point it follows caller.py instead. Its docstring adds 'The path form carries at least one character before the final /vsdd', and the code has 'len(word) <= 5'. The spec says nothing of the kind. It says the program is vsdd or 'a path of safe characters that ends in /vsdd', holds no '=' and begins with a letter, a digit, '_', '.' or '/'. The word /vsdd meets every one of those conditions. The regex [A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*/vsdd needs a character before the final '/vsdd', so it refuses '/vsdd survey' while it accepts '//vsdd survey', which names the same program. The parsed gate alone would accept '/vsdd survey' (program /vsdd, basename vsdd). No reason is given anywhere for refusing it. I compared my own literal reading of the spec, a deterministic token walk, with the regex over 657,186 texts. These were single-character inserts, replacements and deletions of every base and table row, two-character edits and 300,000 random texts. The two disagree on 283 texts, and every one has the program /vsdd. The fixer's checker agrees with the regex on all of them, because of the added rule. So the fixer's claim that the regex and a spec-faithful checker agree everywhere is not quite true. The differential test now pins a behaviour the spec does not state. A mutant that makes the regex accept /vsdd, with the program head made optional, brings the code in line with the spec text, yet it fails test_grammar_checker_agrees_with_the_allow_list. Refusing the call is the safe side: an agent's '/vsdd survey' passes unmarked, and survey then refuses to start. In practice nothing installs vsdd at '/'. The gap is that the spec and the code disagree and the test hides it.
proposed_resolution: Make the spec and the code say one thing, then let the checker follow the spec. Preferred: accept a bare /vsdd. Change the program alternative to (?:vsdd|(?:[A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*)?/vsdd), drop the 'len(word) <= 5' rule and its docstring sentence from _checker_program_word, and add '/vsdd survey' to ALLOWED_CALLS and DIFFERENTIAL_BASES. A bare /vsdd is a plain absolute path with no special reading in sh, bash, dash or zsh, exactly like //vsdd, which is already accepted. Alternative: if /vsdd must stay refused, state the rule and its reason in caller-identity.md's program bullet, have the checker cite that sentence, and add '/vsdd survey' to REFUSED_CALLS so the rule is named. Either way, re-run the differential and the mutation battery.
